items.title: AURA: Audio-Geometry Conditioned U-Net Refinement with Flow Matching for High-Fidelity Monaural-to-Binaural Synthesis
items.authors: Wenjie Zhang(Harbin Institute of Technology(Shenzhen)); Changjun He(Harbin Institute of Technology(Shenzhen)); Yinghan Cao(Harbin Institute of Technology(Shenzhen)); Shiyun Xu(Harbin Institute of Technology(Shenzhen)); Mingjiang Wang(Harbin Institute of Technology(Shenzhen))
items.abstract: Spatial audio is crucial for immersive listening, and binaural rendering is particularly appealing due to its alignment with human auditory perception. However, synthesizing high-quality binaural audio from monaural input remains challenging, as spatial cues must be inferred while preserving both spatial realism and fine-grained timbral detail, limiting its use in VR/AR and telepresence. To address this issue, we propose AURA, a two-stage binaural synthesis framework that explicitly models the relationship between monaural audio and source direction. The first stage combines global context modeling and local texture extraction to produce a coarse binaural estimate. The second stage refines this estimate with a generative mechanism, enhancing spatial cues and spectral details for high-fidelity output. Extensive experiments show that AURA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both subjective evaluations and objective metrics (Wave-L2: 0.123 vs. 0.128).

items.title: GISNO: Neural Operator-based HRTF Personalization from 3D Meshes via Differentiable Helmholtz Rendering
items.authors: Chen Huang(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Lei Zhou(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Hongqing Liu(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Lu Gan(Brunel University); Liming Shi(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: Individualized head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) are crucial for immersive audio, yet their acquisition remains challenging. Existing deep-learning approaches are often constrained by discrete sampling grids and lose fine morphological details during mesh preprocessing. In this work, we propose a geometrically informed spherical neural operator (GISNO), a framework that reformulates HRTF prediction as a continuous operator-learning problem. By integrating a discretization-invariant neural operator with a differentiable Helmholtz-integral renderer, our model learns to map 3D head geometry to continuous boundary pressure fields. Experiments on the HUTUBS dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms representative baselines in log-spectral distortion. Furthermore, the physics-integrated architecture enables multi-dimensional zero-shot generalization across unseen spatial densities, distances, and frequencies, offering a robust solution for scalable HRTF personalization.

items.title: TTBA: Spatial Prompted Text to Binaural Audio Generation Using Transformer
items.authors: Changjun He(Harbin Institute of Technology); Lianyu Zhou(Harbin Institute of Technology); Yukun Qian(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)); Shiyun Xu(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)); Wenjie Zhang(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)); Mingjiang Wang(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)); Weiping Chen(Harbin Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: Binaural audio can deliver an immersive listening experience, and it is valuable for virtual reality, gaming, and creative content production. While recent text-to-audio models can generate high-fidelity audio, they still struggle to generate binaural signals with directional control and accurate spatial perception. To address this issue, we propose TTBA, a text-to-binaural audio generation model. TTBA combines a cross-arranged discrete representation with a transformer-based autoregressive backbone to jointly model semantic content and spatial cues. We further design a spatial prompt encoder that maps explicit spatial prompts into a conditioning representation, which is fused with text features to guide binaural token generation. We use a monaural generation model as guidance and emphasize both content accuracy and inter-channel discrepancy. Experiments on the BEWO-1M dataset show that TTBA can generate binaural audio with spatial awareness and controllable directionality.

items.title: Spec2Spatial: A Time-Frequency Spatial Attention Network for Binaural Audio Synthesis
items.authors: Changjun He(Harbin Institute of Technology); Wenjie Zhang(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)); Shiyun Xu(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)); Lianyu Zhou(Harbin Institute of Technology); Weiping Chen(Harbin Institute of Technology); Mingjiang Wang(Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen))
items.abstract: Binaural audio can provide realism and immersion, and it is widely used in scenarios such as virtual reality. The difficulty of binaural recording has motivated research on binaural audio synthesis. Deep learning-based binaural synthesis is promising, but existing methods still perform poorly, especially in reproducing interaural differences. In this paper, we propose Spec2Spatial, a time-frequency spatial attention network for binaural audio synthesis. Specifically, we introduce an interaural spatial attention network to capture left-right relations in the frequency domain. Additionally, we propose a condition fusion residual network that uses sound source position to adjust time-frequency features. Experiments on the Binaural Speech dataset show that Spec2Spatial synthesizes realistic binaural audio, achieving state-of-the-art DILD (1.250), DITD (0.034), and MRSTFT (1.174).

items.title: Geometry-Informed Distributed Acoustic Scene Understanding
items.authors: Yiyuan Yang(University of Oxford); Shitong Xu(University of Oxford); Niki Trigoni(University of Oxford); Andrew Markham(University of Oxford)
items.abstract: Acoustic scene understanding in multi-room environments is a difficult task. Most existing systems use a single centralized microphone array, and they often fail because walls and doors block sound signals. To address this challenge, we propose a geometry-informed distributed acoustic scene understanding framework. Our system leverages distributed microphones and uses an audio spectrogram transformer and a topology-aware graph neural network to fuse spatio-temporal acoustic features. Then, these features are decoded into discrete semantic triplets. Finally, a frozen large language model combines these symbolic observations with the environmental geometry. This allows the system to perform spatial understanding, infer plausible missing transitions, and generate a physically consistent narrative of the scene. Experiments on a custom multi-room simulator demonstrate that our framework outperforms centralized baselines and improves spatial consistency under simulated occlusion.

items.title: Branch-wise Complementary Attention for Acoustic Scene Classification
items.authors: Seung-Gyu Han(Hanyang University); Jinwoo Jung(Hanyang University); Pil Moo Byun(Hanyang University); Won-Gook Choi(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea)
items.abstract: Acoustic scene classification (ASC) requires lightweight models that effectively capture diverse temporal and spectral cues for mobile devices. Multi-branch convolutional architectures improve receptive field diversity, but their outputs are typically aggregated without explicitly modeling complementary relationships or compensating for branch-specific limitations. We propose a branch-wise complementary attention (BCA) module that allocates channel, time, frequency, and joint time-frequency attention maps across branches according to their receptive field characteristics. By explicitly addressing the inherent limitations of each branch, BCA enhances multi-scale feature integration beyond simple aggregation. Integrated into the Rep-Mobile backbone, BCA consistently outperforms existing attention mechanisms on the TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2020 and 2022 Mobile benchmarks.

items.title: CoSTALA: Compositional Spatio-Temporal Audio-Language Alignment via Multi-Grain Hierarchical Contrastive Learning
items.authors: Peiwei Ren(Xi’an Jiaotong Liverpool University); Jinbo Hu(Xiaomi Inc.); Fang Kang(University of Oulu); Shan Liang(Xi’an Jiaotong Liverpool University); Yin Cao(Chinese Academy of Sciences)
items.abstract: Conventional audio language models (ALMs) have made significant progress in achieving alignment between auditory and textual representations, including recent explorations in spatial audio. However, in daily spatial scenarios, they still cannot effectively process multi-event audio sequences. Current approaches primarily rely on coarse-grained contrastive learning with global auditory and textual features, lacking the resolution to distinguish multiple sequential events. To overcome these limitations, we propose CoSTALA—a novel training paradigm that transitions from purely global alignment to fine-grained spatio-temporal reasoning. By constructing a multi-granularity hierarchical loss function system, we achieve explicit modeling of temporal dependencies, and successfully anchors individual acoustic events to preserve their semantic purity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoSTALA significantly establish a powerful new framework for spatio-temporal audio understanding.

items.title: Perceptually Weighted Minimum Mean Square Error Precoding for Acoustic Multi-User MIMO in Vehicular Personal Sound Zones
items.authors: Huihui Wei( Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Dengke Deng(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Pengcheng Luo(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Weiyu You(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Xiaojuan Zhang(Institute of Advanced Intelligence and Computing); Genke Yang(Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
items.abstract: To address multiuser interference in in-vehicle personal sound zones (PSZ), this paper proposes a perceptually weighted acoustic multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) precoding framework. Traditional spatial audio methods often neglect human psychoacoustics, treating cross-talk merely as uniform physical energy. To overcome this, we integrate a psychoacoustic masking model into the Weighted Minimum Mean Square Error (WMMSE) criterion. The algorithm dynamically assigns stronger distortion penalties to perceptually sensitive time-frequency regions while relaxing constraints in zones heavily masked by target speech. By actively coordinating precoding filters, this method minimizes the perceptually weighted MSE, jointly balancing inter-user interference and target-signal distortion. Validated using measured impulse responses from a real car cabin, the approach shows improvements in objective speech quality over baselines, offering a scalable solution for smart cockpit audio.

items.title: SA-HRTF: A Sound-Assisted Approach to Personalized HRTF Modeling
items.authors: Qingyin Zhao(Inner Mongolia University); Siyuan Chen(Inner Mongolia University); De Hu(Inner Mongolia University)
items.abstract: Head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) are essential for immersive binaural audio rendering, whereas generic HRTFs are often inadequate for accurately reproducing individual spatial cues. Although neural-network-based personalized HRTF modeling has progressed rapidly, accurate reconstruction under sparse measurements remains challenging because limited spatial information hinders reliable estimation. To address this issue, we propose a sound-assisted HRTF (SA-HRTF) model that incorporates binaural acoustic information into personalized HRTF estimation. The proposed architecture adopts a dual-branch design: the primary branch exploits structural features from an existing database to generate an initial estimate, while the auxiliary branch extracts perceptual cues from sound signals to provide supplementary predictions. A fusion module combines the outputs of the two branches to produce a more accurate personalized HRTF. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

items.title: Bayesian Model-Based Assessment of Spatial and Source Priors in Sagittal-Plane Sound Localization
items.authors: Yunda Chen(Shenzhen University); Nengheng Zheng(Shenzhen University)
items.abstract: Sagittal-plane localization in the polar dimension is ill-posed, entangling unknown source spectra and head-related transfer functions. Humans may resolve this ambiguity through sensory evidence and learned priors. We evaluated these priors using a Bayesian observer with an ecological source prior and five spatial priors. Models were calibrated against human responses across cochlear implant (CI)-like reductions in spectral resolution. Across conditions, the models captured the decrease in polar and quadrant errors as spectral resolution improved. The ecological source prior provided limited additional benefit within the present model implementation, whereas predictions were more sensitive to spatial-prior configuration. No single spatial prior was consistently preferred, although asymmetric variants showed better overall agreement with human data. These findings support individualized modeling of spatial hearing under reduced spectral resolution.
